instantiated_cells.justification: Section 305.003(a)(2) requires registration if a person receives (or is entitled to receive) compensation or reimbursement of more than an amount set by commission rule but not less than $200 in a calendar quarter for lobbying communications.

Section 305.003(a)(1) requires registration if a person makes total lobbying-related expenditures of an amount determined by commission rule but not less than $200 in a calendar quarter (excluding the person’s own travel/food/lodging and own dues).

unscoreable_emissions.reason: The statute sets thresholds for when additional details must be included (e.g., gifts over $50; food/entertainment/transport over 60% of legislative per diem), but does not establish a general per-item de minimis below which an expenditure need not be reported at all under §305.006(b).

The statute requires registered lobbyists to file activity reports (§305.006, §305.007) and allows a modified reporting option below $1,000/year (§305.0063), but it does not provide an exemption from filing disclosure entirely based on total expenditures; commission-rule thresholds could apply but are not in the provided text.
The statute provides an hours-based de minimis registration exception (§305.003(b-3)), but does not set an exemption keyed to a percentage of an individual’s compensated time.

arguments.justification: Section 305.003(b-3) provides that Subsection (a)(2) does not require registration if the person spends not more than 26 hours (or other amount by commission) in the quarter on compensated/reimbursed lobbying activity, with §305.003(b-4) addressing daily hour counting.
